title: Impact of Merit Scholarships on College Enrollment

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
I will use Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) since we have a clear cutoff (GPA threshold) that determines treatment assignment (merit scholarship eligibility). The key assumption is that students cannot precisely manipulate their GPA around the cutoff, creating quasi-random assignment to treatment. I'll estimate the local average treatment effect by comparing students just above and below the GPA threshold.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(rdrobust)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s85_data.csv")

# Check data structure
print("Data summary:")
print(summary(data))

# Determine the cutoff (where treatment switches from 0 to 1)
cutoff <- 0.5  # Based on the data preview, appears to be around 0.5

# Main RDD estimation using rdrobust
rd_result <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                      x = data$running_var, 
                      c = cutoff)

# Print main results
print("=== MAIN RDD RESULTS ===")
print(paste("Treatment Effect (RD Estimate):", round(rd_result$coef[1], 4)))
print(paste("Standard Error:", round(rd_result$se[1], 4)))
print(paste("P-value:", round(rd_result$pv[1], 4)))
print(paste("95% Confidence Interval: [", 
            round(rd_result$ci[1,1], 4), ", ", 
            round(rd_result$ci[1,2], 4), "]"))

# Bandwidth information
print(paste("Optimal bandwidth:", round(rd_result$bws[1], 4)))
print(paste("Number of observations used:", rd_result$N[1]))

# Robustness checks
print("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===")

# 1. Alternative bandwidth (half and double)
rd_half_bw <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = cutoff, 
                       h = rd_result$bws[1] * 0.5)
rd_double_bw <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = cutoff, 
                         h = rd_result$bws[1] * 2)

print(paste("Half bandwidth estimate:", round(rd_half_bw$coef[1], 4)))
print(paste("Double bandwidth estimate:", round(rd_double_bw$coef[1], 4)))

# 2. Different polynomial orders
rd_poly2 <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = cutoff, p = 2)
print(paste("Quadratic polynomial estimate:", round(rd_poly2$coef[1], 4)))

# 3. McCrary density test for manipulation
density_test <- rddensity(data$running_var, c = cutoff)
print(paste("McCrary test p-value:", round(density_test$test$p_jk, 4)))

# Create visualization
# Prepare data for plotting
data$running_var_centered <- data$running_var - cutoff

# Create RDD plot
p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = running_var_centered, y = y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(data = subset(data, running_var_centered < 0), 
              method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(data = subset(data, running_var_centered >= 0), 
              method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "blue") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", size = 1) +
  labs(title = "RDD Plot: Merit Scholarship Impact on College Enrollment",
       x = "GPA (centered at cutoff)",
       y = "College Enrollment") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p)

# Summary statistics by treatment status
print("\n=== SUMMARY BY TREATMENT STATUS ===")
treated_stats <- aggregate(data$y, by = list(data$treated), FUN = function(x) c(mean = mean(x), sd = sd(x), n = length(x)))
print(treated_stats)

print(paste("Raw difference in means:", 
            round(mean(data$y[data$treated == 1]) - mean(data$y[data$treated == 0]), 4)))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive treatment effect of approximately 0.3-0.6 on college enrollment rates. Merit scholarships should significantly increase the probability of college enrollment by reducing financial barriers. The magnitude should be substantial since financial aid is a key determinant of college access, particularly for students near the eligibility threshold who likely face budget constraints. The effect should be statistically significant given the clear financial incentive created by the scholarship program.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: The analysis exploits the GPA threshold as a cutoff to compare students just above and below the threshold.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Meeting the GPA threshold for a merit scholarship significantly increases college enrollment rates.
